description: VCO with sine, triangle, saw and square outputs all available at once, forked from Fundamental VCO-1 to use a quarter of the CPU; the maker deprecated it once VCV rewrote the original

params.text: Switches between the digital waveforms and an analogue emulation that softens the sine and adds a little random detuning
Picks the oscillator sync a signal at the sync input triggers, hard or soft
Sets the pitch, plus or minus 54 semitones from C4
Tunes the pitch a semitone up or down
Attenuates the CV at the fm input, which bends the pitch exponentially
Sets the pulse width of the square output, with no effect on the other three waveforms
Attenuates the CV at the pwm input before it is added to the pulse width knob

inputs.text: Sets the pitch, a volt per octave
Bends the pitch through the fm cv knob
Restarts the oscillator's cycle, hard or soft according to the switch
Modulates the pulse width of the square output through the pwm cv knob

outputs.text: The square wave, at the width set by the p width knob

notes: the fm cv and pwm cv knobs come up at zero, so a cable at either modulation input changes nothing until the knob beside it is turned up

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 0.01V · stepped · one channel only
